source.title: Displacement Geometry Captures Platonic Shared Reality Across Models and Modalities
source.authors: Chenming Shang; Yu-Jin Tang; Jun-Jie Ou Yang; Rui-Ze Xu; Adam Breuer; Nikhil Singh

record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests cross-model representational convergence using displacement-vector cosine similarity under orthogonal alignment, rather than the original studies’ pointwise neighborhood or similarity measures. It also argues that pointwise convergence is incomplete.
record.gate_note: The paper reports displacement and pointwise similarity results, scale results, and PCA-dimension comparisons that bear on the claim. The concept-geometry analyses and Shadow Casting benchmark results are not rows because they do not measure the claim versions. Results attributed to cited studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out cross-model alignment using displacement and pointwise cosine, reports a model-size trend, and tests dependence on metric, dimensionality and layer. Static cross-modal alignment does not establish V2's improvement trend.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors argue that models share displacement directions more strongly than pointwise positions, particularly for concepts, and report increasing displacement similarity with model size. They propose shared linear semantic and private capability components and demonstrate a trained capability-transfer method. They leave extreme-scale behavior, uniqueness of the shared geometry and the contribution of overlapping training data unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses cosine similarity between aligned displacement vectors, plus pointwise cosine as a comparator, rather than mutual kNN or the original pointwise-neighborhood measure. It applies PCA, whitening, and a held-out rigid orthogonal Procrustes alignment.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported similarities vary with PCA dimensionality (20, 100, 500), modality grouping, and whether the analysis is sample-level or concept-level. The paper reports that the qualitative ordering is stable across the tested PCA dimensions.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-Object cosine is high even in randomly initialized models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model offsets can have consistent directions across inputs because of architectural structure, without learned representational convergence.

record.problems: The authors state that the analysis does not reach the largest frontier systems, cannot determine whether displacement parallelism strengthens or degrades at extreme scale, and cannot disentangle shared training data from common world structure. The main reported scale trend is not accompanied by exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Left out training-objective experiments in §4.5, decomposition and probe results in §4.6, concept-orthogonality results in §4.2 and App. A.4, simulations in App. A.2, and Shadow Casting benchmark results in §5 and App. E because they do not directly measure the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Capability improvement independently of parameter count, frontier-scale behavior, and generality beyond the reported vision size sweep.
Whether paired image-caption alignment increases as both vision and language models improve; positive static cross-modal alignment alone does not test this trend.
Shared learned features or subspaces across trained networks differing only in initialization; the seed comparison uses untrained controls.

Interchangeability with little functional loss after a simple map, stitching, relative representations or unpaired alignment. Procrustes cosine and the trained ShadowCLIP composition do not establish this.
Recurrence of identifiable neurons, SAE features or circuits across models. Concept-centroid displacement alignment does not identify such units or circuits.
Sensitivity to kNN settings and systematic out-of-distribution evaluation; no tested choice makes displacement alignment vanish in the main pretrained-model comparisons.

Plateauing with scale and causal attribution of naturally occurring convergence to shared training data rather than world structure. Training-data overlap is acknowledged but not experimentally separated.

missing.what: Layer-dependent displacement alignment: vision pairs concentrate near matching depths, language pairs align broadly in middle/deep layers, and language layers align preferentially with deep vision layers.

Pretraining-objective comparison: CLIP and DINO have higher displacement similarity than MAE; holding objective fixed, dataset choice reportedly has little effect. Record as qualitative results rather than inventing numerical differences.

Pointwise scores for asymmetric pairs: CLIP-Huge/MAE-Base 0.059 and Llama3-8B/Bloomz-560M 0.182. Table 2 also reports Llama3-8B/CLIP-Huge pointwise 0.204 and displacement 0.306, a distinct pair from r16.

record.verdict_notes: States for rows linked to V6/V7 describe metric dependence or incomplete alignment, rather than treating every positive cosine as support for scaling. V6 and V7 are challenge claims, so evidence of dependence or incompleteness supports them. The declared exclusions in §§4.5–4.6 include relevant objective-dependence and shared/private-subspace results; they are not listed as missing because rows_left_out explicitly declares them. Distillation-induced alignment should not independently support spontaneous convergence. Table 4 does not identify why its PCA-500 values differ from the main aggregates, and its language results contradict the prose assertion that every metric increases as dimensionality decreases.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not isolate performance gains from model size, and does not test the largest frontier systems. Its main convergence measure is displacement-direction cosine, not similarity between the distances themselves.
The study measures cross-modal alignment on paired image-caption data, but does not establish a scale trend specifically for pairs where both the vision and language models improve.
It does not compare trained networks of the same architecture across initialization seeds for shared features or subspaces.

It uses rigid orthogonal alignment for measurement but does not test whether mapped representations are interchangeable in downstream use, or compare stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mappings.
It does not test whether the same interpretable features or circuits recur across models.
The study varies PCA dimensionality and compares pointwise with displacement similarity, but does not systematically vary kNN settings or test out-of-distribution inputs.
It reports incomplete alignment and discusses overlapping training data, but does not causally separate shared-data effects from common world structure or test whether alignment plateaus.
